architecture_decisions: The implementation plan will focus on refining Parallax's protected validation toolchain to utilize deterministic repository evidence for Python, JavaScript/Node, and .NET applications.
The toolchain will be immutable released policy containing only server-owned values, ensuring consistent execution environments for candidates.
Profile selection will consume only canonical Project/run/lineage-bound server materialization, preventing generic shell command execution or network broadening.
work_items: Research and implement deterministic repository intelligence to recognize representative .NET evidence deterministically.
Establish immutable validation-profile registry/selection contract for Python, Node, and .NET profiles.
Develop candidate validation profile selection/binding to ensure selected profiles are bound to candidate-validation evidence and accepted-lineage BUILD/TEST/VERIFY.
Design focused tests for Python/Node/.NET selection, ambiguity, injection resistance, and candidate/canonical agreement.
validations: Prove that the toolchain remains immutable released policy containing only server-owned values.
Prove that repository intelligence recognizes representative .NET evidence deterministically.
Prove that candidate validation profiles are bound to candidate-validation evidence and accepted-lineage BUILD/TEST/VERIFY.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — Repository intelligence recognizes representative `.sln`, `.csproj`, and C# source evidence deterministically, records bounded evidence identities, and does not execute or trust repository command text.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — Python, Node, and .NET profiles contain only server-owned command templates. Repository/model/user text cannot change executable, argument template, environment, network, provider, Git, deployment, or approval authority.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — An exact source tree produces one stable profile/root identity or a typed unsupported/ambiguous result. Mixed/conflicting roots never trigger guessed execution.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — A representative OT Time-like C# repository selects the .NET profile and candidate BUILD/TEST/VERIFY use fixed `dotnet` invocations against the admitted solution/project identity instead of Parallax pytest paths.
AC-05: validate protected requirement — Representative existing Python/Parallax fixtures retain protected BUILD/TEST/VERIFY behavior and all inherited execution-policy tests remain green.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — A representative Node repository is either validated through a fixed admitted Node profile or explicitly rejected when safe offline fixed commands cannot be proven. Repository `scripts` values never become command authority.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — The selected validation profile identity is bound to candidate-validation evidence and accepted-lineage BUILD/TEST/VERIFY; canonical execution cannot silently switch profile/toolchain after candidate admission.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Missing executable, pinned-snapshot toolchain, or offline dependency returns bounded non-success evidence and performs no source-lineage acceptance, network/package installation, provider mutation, or deployment mutation.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Project/spec/run identity, single-writer source acceptance, immutable lineage, evaluator precedence, tenant/auth, source-only handoff, Vercel Preview delivery, provider scopes, and REVIEW boundaries do not regress.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — After exact release deployment, a QA-owned source-only Project bound to `github:Ryan9876/ot-time` progresses from PLAN through IMPLEMENT/BUILD/TEST/VERIFY to REVIEW and the authenticated exact-lineage ZIP handoff verifies, without Vercel deployment target, Vercel repository-provider authorization, out-of-band source edit, owner impersonation, or DB mutation.
risks: Potential for generic shell command execution or network broadening through repository-defined script text.
Potential for missing executable or unavailable offline dependency through toolchain/dependency absence.

critique: The specification highlights several significant improvements to Parallax 2.0 for repository-aware protected validation. Key points include generalizing protected candidate and accepted-lineage validation, extending repository intelligence to recognize .NET solution/project markers, and defining server-owned validation profiles. The specification also outlines security and authority requirements, acceptance criteria, scope, non-goals, and release gate.
